title: bug: PowerShell Invoke-MoeRpc unwraps singleton JSON arrays into objects
description: On Windows PowerShell 5.1, Invoke-MoeRpc's `return ($text | ConvertFrom-Json)` unrolls `[ {profile:'verified-local',ready:true,missingCapabilities:[]} ]` into PSCustomObject (reproduced with its exact return expression). CQ-M07n1's approved downstream object/type predicate cannot distinguish this malformed wire array from a valid readiness object; audit scalar/object RPC consumers and preserve wire shape without changing existing list callers.
reopenReason: Promoted from BACKLOG by the governor under the human's standing "move from backlog" (2026-11-02 21:00Z). worker-26483323 filed it from CQ-M07n1 (msg-43f05c7a), and it has no dependsOn. The human can drag it back to BACKLOG to veto. Governor ruling on n1, comment on task-65b3e023: n1 hands this defect forward, and this row fixes Invoke-MoeRpc's singleton-array unrolling on its own.

comments.content:
Architect note (16:55Z): I added dependsOn task-65b3e023 (CQ-M07n1). This departs from the governor's "no dependsOn edge" placement, for a reason that note did not cover.

This is a PRODUCES edge under the §8 rule (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §8), not a file-only edge:
- The deferred row goes into scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.ps1, which n1 creates.
- The row exercises Invoke-MoeVerifiedLocalGate, the gate n1 adds.
- In worktree mode this row's worktree is cut once, at its first WORKING claim, and later sessions reuse it. TURBO makes the row claimable the moment the plan lands. A claim before n1 lands would get a base that has neither file, with no way for the worker to pull them in.

The early-start practice from n1/m1 applies: once n1's completion is on moe/work-2026-10-24, the edge can be dropped before n1 reaches DONE. The plan's step 1 re-checks that the base holds n1's bytes, and blocks on task-65b3e023 if not.

Plan basis:
- The fix stays inside Invoke-MoeRpc. n1's gate needs no edit: a singleton array now reaches it as an array, and its PSCustomObject check sends it down today's path, the same route the sh twin takes.
- I dry-ran it on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7 in a scratch copy of n1's current files: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-044c/.
